claim: The export of mRNA from nucleus to cytoplasm requires the conserved and essential transcription and export (TREX) complex (THO–UAP56/DDX39B–ALYREF).
source: The export of mRNA from nucleus to cytoplasm requires the conserved and essential transcription and export (TREX) complex (THO–UAP56/DDX39B–ALYREF).
evidence: This is a foundational statement about TREX complex function, supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: TREX selectively binds mRNA maturation marks and licenses mRNA for nuclear export by loading the export factor NXF1–NXT1.
source: TREX selectively binds mRNA maturation marks and licenses mRNA for nuclear export by loading the export factor NXF1–NXT1.
evidence: This describes the known function of TREX based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: The cryo-electron microscopy structure of the human THO–UAP56/DDX39B complex was determined at 3.3 Å resolution.
source: Here, we report the cryo-electron microscopy structure of the human THO–UAP56/DDX39B complex at 3.3 Å resolution.
evidence: This is directly supported by the experimental cryo-EM data presented in the manuscript, including resolution statistics in Figure 1—figure supplement 3a and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The seven-subunit THO–UAP56/DDX39B complex multimerizes into a 28-subunit tetrameric assembly.
source: The seven-subunit THO–UAP56/DDX39B complex multimerizes into a 28-subunit tetrameric assembly, suggesting that selective recognition of mature mRNA is facilitated by the simultaneous sensing of multiple, spatially distant mRNA regions and maturation marks.
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structure data showing the tetrameric architecture (Figures 1a–c and 2).

claim: Selective recognition of mature mRNA is facilitated by the simultaneous sensing of multiple, spatially distant mRNA regions and maturation marks.
source: The seven-subunit THO–UAP56/DDX39B complex multimerizes into a 28-subunit tetrameric assembly, suggesting that selective recognition of mature mRNA is facilitated by the simultaneous sensing of multiple, spatially distant mRNA regions and maturation marks.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed tetrameric structure and its extended architecture.

claim: Two UAP56/DDX39B RNA helicases are juxtaposed at each end of the tetramer.
source: Two UAP56/DDX39B RNA helicases are juxtaposed at each end of the tetramer, which would allow one bivalent ALYREF protein to bridge adjacent helicases and regulate the TREX–mRNA interaction.
evidence: This is directly observed in the cryo-EM structure (Figure 1c, Figure 4b).

claim: One bivalent ALYREF protein can bridge adjacent UAP56 helicases and regulate the TREX–mRNA interaction.
source: Two UAP56/DDX39B RNA helicases are juxtaposed at each end of the tetramer, which would allow one bivalent ALYREF protein to bridge adjacent helicases and regulate the TREX–mRNA interaction.
evidence: This is a speculative model based on the structural positioning of UAP56 helicases and known ALYREF binding properties.

claim: Eukaryotic protein-coding mRNA is matured in the nucleus before it is exported and translated in the cytoplasm.
source: Eukaryotic protein-coding mRNA is matured in the nucleus before it is exported and translated in the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about eukaryotic gene expression, supported by citations (Köhler and Hurt, 2007; Singh et al., 2015; Heath et al., 2016; Stewart, 2019; Xie and Ren, 2019).

claim: During maturation, mRNA is capped, spliced, and poly-adenylated to form fully processed and packaged messenger ribonucleoprotein complexes (mRNPs).
source: During maturation, mRNA is capped, spliced, and poly-adenylated to form fully processed and packaged messenger ribonucleoprotein complexes (mRNPs) (Köhler and Hurt, 2007; Singh et al., 2015; Heath et al., 2016; Stewart, 2019; Xie and Ren, 2019).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The transcription and export (TREX) complex is recruited during transcription to maturing mRNPs through mRNA and protein interactions at the mRNP 5'-end, splice junctions, and mRNP 3'-end.
source: The transcription and export (TREX) complex is recruited during transcription (Heath et al., 2016; Viphakone et al., 2019) to maturing mRNPs through mRNA and protein interactions at the mRNP 5'-end, splice junctions, and mRNP 3'-end (Cheng et al., 2006; Merz et al., 2007; Gromadzka et al., 2016; Shi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations describing TREX recruitment mechanisms.

claim: TREX subsequently loads the global mRNA-export factor NXF1–NXT1, to license mRNAs for export.
source: TREX subsequently loads the global mRNA-export factor NXF1–NXT1, to license mRNAs for export (Strässer and Hurt, 2001; Köhler and Hurt, 2007; Hautbergue et al., 2008; Taniguchi and Ohno, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations describing TREX function in export factor loading.

claim: By chaperoning the nascent mRNA, TREX also inhibits the formation of harmful DNA-RNA hybrids, called R-loops, and protects genome integrity.
source: By chaperoning the nascent mRNA, TREX also inhibits the formation of harmful DNA-RNA hybrids, called R-loops, and protects genome integrity (Luna et al., 2019; Pérez-Calero et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing TREX's role in preventing R-loop formation.

claim: The TREX complex is found in all eukaryotes.
source: The TREX complex is found in all eukaryotes and contains the multi-subunit THO complex, the DEXD-box RNA helicase UAP56/DDX39B (yeast Sub2), and an RNA export adapter such as ALYREF (yeast Yra1) (Strässer et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation describing TREX conservation across eukaryotes.

claim: The TREX complex contains the multi-subunit THO complex, the DEXD-box RNA helicase UAP56/DDX39B (yeast Sub2), and an RNA export adapter such as ALYREF (yeast Yra1).
source: The TREX complex is found in all eukaryotes and contains the multi-subunit THO complex, the DEXD-box RNA helicase UAP56/DDX39B (yeast Sub2), and an RNA export adapter such as ALYREF (yeast Yra1) (Strässer et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation describing TREX composition.

claim: The human THO complex comprises six subunits, THOC1, −2, –3, −5, –6, and −7.
source: The human THO complex comprises six subunits, THOC1, −2, –3, −5, –6, and −7, of which four have known counterparts in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Sc): THOC1 (yeast Hpr1), −2 (yeast Tho2), −3 (yeast Tex3), and −7 (yeast Mft1) (Heath et al., 2016; Mitchell et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing THO complex composition.

claim: Four human THO subunits have known counterparts in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae: THOC1 (yeast Hpr1), −2 (yeast Tho2), −3 (yeast Tex3), and −7 (yeast Mft1).
source: The human THO complex comprises six subunits, THOC1, −2, –3, −5, –6, and −7, of which four have known counterparts in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Sc): THOC1 (yeast Hpr1), −2 (yeast Tho2), −3 (yeast Tex3), and −7 (yeast Mft1) (Heath et al., 2016; Mitchell et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing homology between human and yeast THO subunits.

claim: Additional TREX interactors include SARNP (yeast Tho1), the mammalian protein ZC3H11A and ALYREF-like proteins UIF, LUZP4, POLDIP3, and CHTOP.
source: Additional TREX interactors include SARNP (yeast Tho1), the mammalian protein ZC3H11A and ALYREF-like proteins UIF, LUZP4, POLDIP3, and CHTOP (Dufu et al., 2010; Heath et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing additional TREX-associated proteins.

claim: In the current model of mRNA export, the THO complex is recruited to the mRNP and delivers UAP56, which subsequently 'clamps' the mRNA.
source: In the current model of mRNA export, the THO complex is recruited to the mRNP and delivers UAP56, which subsequently 'clamps' the mRNA.
evidence: This describes the prevailing model in the field based on established knowledge.

claim: THO–UAP56 binds the export adapter ALYREF and together they promote loading of the export factor NXF1–NXT1 onto mRNA.
source: THO–UAP56 binds the export adapter ALYREF and together they promote loading of the export factor NXF1–NXT1 onto mRNA (Hautbergue et al., 2008; Köhler and Hurt, 2007; Strässer and Hurt, 2001; Taniguchi and Ohno, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations describing the mechanism of export factor loading.

claim: The structural basis for TREX activities remains poorly understood despite active study.
source: However, the structural basis for TREX activities remains poorly understood despite active study (Peña et al., 2012; Pérez-Alvarado et al., 2003; Ren et al., 2017; Shi et al., 2004; Xie and Ren, 2019).
evidence: This is an assessment of the state of the field supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: The human THO complex was prepared by co-expressing its six subunits in insect cells (THOC1, −2 residues 1–1203, −3, –5, −6,–7).
source: To gain structural insights into TREX function, we prepared the human THO complex by co-expressing its six subunits in insect cells (THOC1, −2 residues 1–1203, −3, –5, −6,–7) and added recombinant UAP56 to reconstitute the THO–UAP56 complex (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a, Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used to prepare the complex for structural studies.

claim: Recombinant UAP56 was added to reconstitute the THO–UAP56 complex.
source: To gain structural insights into TREX function, we prepared the human THO complex by co-expressing its six subunits in insect cells (THOC1, −2 residues 1–1203, −3, –5, −6,–7) and added recombinant UAP56 to reconstitute the THO–UAP56 complex (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a, Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used to prepare the complex for structural studies.

claim: The complex was imaged under cryogenic conditions using a K3 direct electron detector, yielding ~1.6 million single-particle images.
source: The complex was imaged under cryogenic conditions using a K3 direct electron detector, yielding ~1.6 million single-particle images.
evidence: This describes the cryo-EM data collection method and results.

claim: Unsupervised 3D particle sorting and focused refinements resulted in cryo-EM densities of THO–UAP56 at nominal resolutions between 3.3 and 4.7 Å (maps A-E).
source: Unsupervised 3D particle sorting and focused refinements resulted in cryo-EM densities of THO–UAP56 at nominal resolutions between 3.3 and 4.7 Å (maps A-E) (Figure 1—figure supplements 1–4, Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the image processing results and resolution achieved.

claim: The densities enabled building a near-complete atomic model of a 14-subunit THO–UAP56 dimer, which assembles into a 28-subunit tetramer with a total molecular weight of 1.8 MDa.
source: The densities enabled us to build a near-complete atomic model of a 14-subunit THO–UAP56 dimer, which assembles into a 28-subunit tetramer with a total molecular weight of 1.8 MDa (Figures 1a–c and 2, Figure 1—figure supplements 5 and 6, Video 1).
evidence: This describes the structural model built from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The cryo-EM data showed that two THO–UAP56 tetramers associate loosely to form an octamer.
source: The cryo-EM data showed that two THO–UAP56 tetramers associate loosely to form an octamer, however, we could not observe direct molecular contacts between the two tetramers (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c,d).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM data analysis.

claim: No direct molecular contacts were observed between the two tetramers in the octamer.
source: The cryo-EM data showed that two THO–UAP56 tetramers associate loosely to form an octamer, however, we could not observe direct molecular contacts between the two tetramers (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c,d).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM data analysis.

claim: The endogenous THO–UAP56 complex was purified from human K562 cells.
source: To determine the in vivo oligomeric state of THO–UAP56, we in addition purified the endogenous complex from human K562 cells and calculated negative stain 2D class averages (Figure 1—figure supplement 1f–h).
evidence: This describes the experimental method to validate the oligomeric state in vivo.

claim: The endogenous THO–UAP56 complex formed a tetramer, indistinguishable from the modeled tetramer structure.
source: The endogenous THO–UAP56 complex formed a tetramer, indistinguishable from the modeled tetramer structure, suggesting that this state exists in vivo (Figure 1—figure supplement 1h).
evidence: This is supported by negative stain EM data of the endogenous complex.

claim: The tetrameric state of THO–UAP56 exists in vivo.
source: The endogenous THO–UAP56 complex formed a tetramer, indistinguishable from the modeled tetramer structure, suggesting that this state exists in vivo (Figure 1—figure supplement 1h).
evidence: This is an inference based on the negative stain EM data of the endogenous complex matching the recombinant structure.

claim: The THO–UAP56 28-subunit tetramer consists of two asymmetric dimers, 1 and 2, each comprising two seven-subunit THO–UAP56 monomers, A and B.
source: The THO–UAP56 28-subunit tetramer consists of two asymmetric dimers, 1 and 2, each comprising two seven-subunit THO–UAP56 monomers, A and B.
evidence: This describes the structural organization observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: Each THO–UAP56 monomer is partitioned into two regions, one formed by THOC1, −2, –3, and UAP56 and the second by THOC5, −6, and −7.
source: Each monomer is partitioned into two regions, one formed by THOC1, −2, –3, and UAP56 and the second by THOC5, −6, and −7.
evidence: This describes the structural organization observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: THOC1, −2, –3, and UAP56 adopt the same architecture in all monomers.
source: THOC1, −2, –3, and UAP56 adopt the same architecture in all monomers, whereas THOC5, −6, –7 assume different conformations to assemble the dimer via THOC5 and THOC7 and the tetramer via THOC5 and THOC6.
evidence: This describes the structural organization observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: THOC5, −6, –7 assume different conformations to assemble the dimer via THOC5 and THOC7 and the tetramer via THOC5 and THOC6.
source: THOC1, −2, –3, and UAP56 adopt the same architecture in all monomers, whereas THOC5, −6, –7 assume different conformations to assemble the dimer via THOC5 and THOC7 and the tetramer via THOC5 and THOC6.
evidence: This describes the structural organization observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: THOC5 and THOC7 form a parallel coiled coil, whose C-terminal ends from monomer A and B meet in a four-helix bundle, yielding the dimerization region.
source: THOC5 and THOC7 form a parallel coiled coil, whose C-terminal ends from monomer A and B meet in a four-helix bundle, yielding the dimerization region (Figures 2 and 3a,b).
evidence: This describes the structural organization observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The dimer is further stabilized by contacts between the N-terminal THOC5 tandem RWD (tRWD-N) domains from monomers A and B that pack against each other.
source: The dimer is further stabilized by contacts between the N-terminal THOC5 tandem RWD (tRWD-N) domains from monomers A and B that pack against each other.
evidence: This describes the structural organization observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The THOC5–THOC7 coiled coil is interrupted by a 'hinge' in each monomer, which generates three mobile sub-regions in the 14-subunit THO–UAP56 dimer: monomer A, monomer B, and the dimerization region.
source: The THOC5–THOC7 coiled coil is interrupted by a 'hinge' in each monomer, which generates three mobile sub-regions in the 14-subunit THO–UAP56 dimer: monomer A, monomer B, and the above mentioned dimerization region (Figures 2 and 3a).
evidence: This describes the structural organization and flexibility observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The THOC5–THOC7 coiled coil measures ~ 350 Å across the human dimer.
source: Notably, the THOC5–THOC7 coiled coil measures ~ 350 Å across the human dimer, suggesting that distal positioning of monomers A and B may play a role in TREX function.
evidence: This is a measurement from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: Distal positioning of monomers A and B may play a role in TREX function.
source: Notably, the THOC5–THOC7 coiled coil measures ~ 350 Å across the human dimer, suggesting that distal positioning of monomers A and B may play a role in TREX function.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed structural dimensions.

claim: The THO–UAP56 tetramer assembles from dimer 1 and 2 via two interfaces that involve the THOC5 and THOC6 subunits.
source: The THO–UAP56 tetramer assembles from dimer 1 and 2 via two interfaces that involve the THOC5 and THOC6 subunits.
evidence: This describes the structural organization observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The first tetramer interface is formed by homotypic interactions between the THOC5 tRWD-C domains from monomers 1A and 2A.
source: The first interface is formed by homotypic interactions between the THOC5 tRWD-C domains from monomers 1A and 2A.
evidence: This describes the structural organization observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The second tetramer interface is formed by the THOC6 β-propeller from monomers 1A and 2A that interact with the THOC1, −5, and −7 subunits from monomers 2B and 1B, respectively.
source: The second is formed by the THOC6 β-propeller from monomers 1A and 2A that interact with the THOC1, −5, and −7 subunits from monomers 2B and 1B, respectively (Figure 3a–c).
evidence: This describes the structural organization observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: THOC6 associates with the neighboring dimer and causes THOC1 and the THOC5–THOC7 coiled coil to adopt different positions.
source: THOC6 thereby associates with the neighboring dimer and causes THOC1 and the THOC5–THOC7 coiled coil to adopt different positions (Figure 3c).
evidence: This describes the structural organization observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: THOC6 interaction stabilizes the tetramer and leads to the asymmetry within the THO–UAP56 dimer.
source: This interaction stabilizes the tetramer and at the same time leads to the asymmetry within the THO–UAP56 dimer (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed structural organization.

claim: The recombinant THO complex lacking THOC6 assembles into a dimer rather than a tetramer.
source: In agreement with this architecture, the recombinant THO complex lacking THOC6 assembles into a dimer rather than a tetramer, shown by its slowed migration in sucrose density gradients (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is supported by biochemical data from sucrose density gradient experiments.

claim: Deletion of the THOC5 and THOC7 subunits leads to loss of THOC6 and results in a monomeric THOC1/2/3 complex.
source: Deletion of the THOC5 and THOC7 subunits leads to loss of THOC6, as expected, and results in a monomeric THOC1/2/3 complex (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is supported by biochemical data from sucrose density gradient experiments.

claim: Nine residues in THOC6 are known to be mutated in human disease.
source: Nine residues in THOC6 are known to be mutated in human disease (Heath et al., 2016), all of which map to the THOC6 β-propeller.
evidence: This is supported by citation to known disease mutations.

claim: All nine disease-associated THOC6 mutations map to the THOC6 β-propeller.
source: Nine residues in THOC6 are known to be mutated in human disease (Heath et al., 2016), all of which map to the THOC6 β-propeller.
evidence: This is an observation based on mapping known mutations onto the structure.

claim: THOC6 disease mutations are predicted to destabilize the β-propeller fold or the THOC5–THOC7 interaction and would thereby disrupt THO tetramerization.
source: These mutations are predicted to destabilize the β-propeller fold or the THOC5–THOC7 interaction and would thereby disrupt THO tetramerization (Figure 2—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is a prediction based on the structural location of disease mutations.

claim: Four THOC6 mutations were previously shown to reduce nuclear THOC6 levels and perturb THOC6 interaction with the THO complex.
source: Indeed, four mutations were previously shown to reduce nuclear THOC6 levels and perturb THOC6 interaction with the THO complex (Mattioli et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous experimental work.

claim: The core of the THO–UAP56 monomer is formed by the THOC2 subunit.
source: The core of the THO–UAP56 monomer is formed by the THOC2 subunit, which comprises an extended helical repeat with five distinct domains that we name 'anchor', 'bow', 'MIF4G', 'stern', and the disordered 'charged domain' (CD, truncated for recombinant expression) (Peña et al., 2012; Figures 1a and 4a).
evidence: This describes the structural organization observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: THOC2 comprises an extended helical repeat with five distinct domains named 'anchor', 'bow', 'MIF4G', 'stern', and the disordered 'charged domain' (CD).
source: The core of the THO–UAP56 monomer is formed by the THOC2 subunit, which comprises an extended helical repeat with five distinct domains that we name 'anchor', 'bow', 'MIF4G', 'stern', and the disordered 'charged domain' (CD, truncated for recombinant expression) (Peña et al., 2012; Figures 1a and 4a).
evidence: This describes the structural organization observed in the cryo-EM structure, with the CD domain previously characterized.

claim: The N-terminal THOC2 anchor helices bind α-helices THOC5 α3 and THOC7 α2.
source: The N-terminal THOC2 anchor helices bind α-helices THOC5 α3 and THOC7 α2 and connect via a disordered linker to the THOC2 bow domain.
evidence: This describes the structural organization observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The THOC2 bow is sandwiched by the helical THOC1 'dock' domain.
source: The THOC2 bow is sandwiched by the helical THOC1 'dock' domain (Figure 3b).
evidence: This describes the structural organization observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The THOC1, −5, and −7 subunits jointly bind THOC2, and THOC1 orients the extended and mobile THOC2 helical repeat (bow, MIF4G, stern).
source: Hence, the THOC1, −5, and −7 subunits jointly bind THOC2, and THOC1 orients the extended and mobile THOC2 helical repeat (bow, MIF4G, stern) (Figures 1c and 2, Figure 1—figure supplements 1d and 3c).
evidence: This describes the structural organization observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The THOC2 bow and adjacent MIF4G domain bind the THOC3 β-propeller.
source: The THOC2 bow and adjacent MIF4G domain bind the THOC3 β-propeller (Figure 4a), and the THOC2 MIF4G domain makes additional, extensive contacts to the UAP56 helicase (Figures 1a and 4a).
evidence: This describes the structural organization observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The THOC2 MIF4G domain makes extensive contacts to the UAP56 helicase.
source: The THOC2 bow and adjacent MIF4G domain bind the THOC3 β-propeller (Figure 4a), and the THOC2 MIF4G domain makes additional, extensive contacts to the UAP56 helicase (Figures 1a and 4a).
evidence: This describes the structural organization observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: UAP56 contains two ATPase lobes, RecA1 and RecA2.
source: UAP56 contains two ATPase lobes, RecA1 and RecA2.
evidence: This is established knowledge about UAP56 structure.

claim: Density was observed for the UAP56 RecA2 lobe, but not RecA1, which remains mobile in the absence of RNA and ATP.
source: We observed density for the UAP56 RecA2 lobe, but not RecA1, which remains mobile in the absence of RNA and ATP (Shi et al., 2004).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM data, with the mobility of RecA1 supported by citation.

claim: THO oligomeric state did not impact UAP56 binding in a pulldown experiment.
source: Consistent with the structure, THO oligomeric state did not impact UAP56 binding in a pulldown experiment (Figure 2—figure supplement 1c), whereas point mutations in the THOC2 MIF4G domain at the UAP56 interface did impair UAP56 binding (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d,e).
evidence: This is supported by biochemical pulldown data.

claim: Point mutations in the THOC2 MIF4G domain at the UAP56 interface impaired UAP56 binding.
source: Consistent with the structure, THO oligomeric state did not impact UAP56 binding in a pulldown experiment (Figure 2—figure supplement 1c), whereas point mutations in the THOC2 MIF4G domain at the UAP56 interface did impair UAP56 binding (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d,e).
evidence: This is supported by biochemical pulldown data.

claim: The THOC2 MIF4G domain adjoins the curved THOC2 stern domain, which in turn connects to the disordered CD implicated in nucleic acid binding.
source: The THOC2 MIF4G domain adjoins the curved THOC2 stern domain, which in turn connects to the disordered CD implicated in nucleic acid binding (Peña et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the structural organization, with the CD function supported by citation.

claim: Weak density was observed for the THOC1 C-terminus near the THOC2 stern.
source: Near the THOC2 stern, we observed weak density for the THOC1 C-terminus (Figure 4a), which can bind the mRNA-export factor in yeast and humans (Hobeika et al., 2007; Viphakone et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM data.

claim: The THOC1 C-terminus can bind the mRNA-export factor in yeast and humans.
source: Near the THOC2 stern, we observed weak density for the THOC1 C-terminus (Figure 4a), which can bind the mRNA-export factor in yeast and humans (Hobeika et al., 2007; Viphakone et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The close positioning of UAP56, the THOC1 C-terminus, and the THOC2 CD suggests that this region is involved in export factor loading.
source: The close positioning of UAP56, the THOC1 C-terminus, and the THOC2 CD suggests that this region is involved in export factor loading.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural positioning of these elements.

claim: The recombinant core THOC1/2/3–UAP56 complex is sufficient to bind the NXF1–NXT1 export factor in vitro.
source: Supporting this model, we observed that the recombinant core THOC1/2/3–UAP56 complex is sufficient to bind the NXF1–NXT1 export factor in vitro (Figure 2—figure supplement 1f).
evidence: This is supported by biochemical pulldown data.

claim: The isolated THOC5 subunit can bind NXF1–NXT1 in vitro.
source: Previous data showed that the isolated THOC5 subunit can also bind NXF1–NXT1 in vitro (Katahira et al., 2009; Viphakone et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: THOC5 did not contribute to NXF1–NXT1 binding in the context of multi-subunit THO–UAP56 complexes.
source: However, THOC5 did not contribute to NXF1–NXT1 binding in the context of multi-subunit THO–UAP56 complexes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1f), consistent with its distant location from the putative export factor loading site in the THO–UAP56 structure (Figures 1c and 4a).
evidence: This is supported by biochemical pulldown data and structural observations.

claim: The THO–UAP56 tetramer is ~260 Å long, ~290 Å high, and ~150 Å wide.
source: The THO–UAP56 tetramer is ~260 Å long,~290 Å high, and ~150 Å wide.
evidence: These are measurements from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: Subunits involved in mRNA and export factor binding are located at the ends of the complex (THOC1, −2, –3, and UAP56), away from those involved in oligomerization (THOC5, −6, and −7).
source: Subunits involved in mRNA and export factor binding are located at the ends of the complex (THOC1, −2, –3, and UAP56), away from those involved in oligomerization (THOC5, −6, and −7) (Figures 1c and 2, Figure 1—figure supplement 6a).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: All THO subunits are essential genes.
source: Whereas all THO subunits are essential genes (Dempster et al., 2019), the requirement for THOC5, −6, and −7 suggests that THO oligomerization may be needed for normal function.
evidence: This is supported by citation to essentiality data.

claim: The requirement for THOC5, −6, and −7 suggests that THO oligomerization may be needed for normal function.
source: Whereas all THO subunits are essential genes (Dempster et al., 2019), the requirement for THOC5, −6, and −7 suggests that THO oligomerization may be needed for normal function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the essentiality of oligomerization subunits.

claim: The extended shape and flexibility of the THO–UAP56 tetramer could allow for multiple interactions with spatially distant mRNA regions and mRNP maturation marks.
source: The extended shape and flexibility of the THO–UAP56 tetramer (Figure 4—figure supplement 1d) could allow for multiple interactions with spatially distant mRNA regions and mRNP maturation marks, such as the cap-binding complex or exon-junction complex (Cheng et al., 2006; Merz et al., 2007) and facilitate NXF1–NXT1 loading from multiple sites.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the structural features and known TREX interactions.

claim: ALYREF (yeast Yra1) is part of the conserved TREX complex.
source: ALYREF (yeast Yra1) is part of the conserved TREX complex (Chávez et al., 2000; Strässer et al., 2002), is required for transfer of mRNA to the export factor NXF1–NXT1 (Hautbergue et al., 2008; Taniguchi and Ohno, 2008), and is essential for viability in yeast (Strässer and Hurt, 2000; Stutz et al., 2000) and humans (Dempster et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: ALYREF is required for transfer of mRNA to the export factor NXF1–NXT1.
source: ALYREF (yeast Yra1) is part of the conserved TREX complex (Chávez et al., 2000; Strässer et al., 2002), is required for transfer of mRNA to the export factor NXF1–NXT1 (Hautbergue et al., 2008; Taniguchi and Ohno, 2008), and is essential for viability in yeast (Strässer and Hurt, 2000; Stutz et al., 2000) and humans (Dempster et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: ALYREF is essential for viability in yeast and humans.
source: ALYREF (yeast Yra1) is part of the conserved TREX complex (Chávez et al., 2000; Strässer et al., 2002), is required for transfer of mRNA to the export factor NXF1–NXT1 (Hautbergue et al., 2008; Taniguchi and Ohno, 2008), and is essential for viability in yeast (Strässer and Hurt, 2000; Stutz et al., 2000) and humans (Dempster et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: ALYREF contains two UAP56-binding motifs (UBMs) at its N- and C-terminus that can separately bind UAP56.
source: ALYREF contains two UAP56-binding motifs (UBMs) at its N- and C-terminus that can separately bind UAP56 (Hautbergue et al., 2009; Figure 4—figure supplement 1a,b).
evidence: This is supported by citation and figure reference.

claim: Between the ALYREF UBMs is an RG-rich region, followed by a central RNA-recognition motif (RRM) domain, and a second RG-rich region.
source: Between the UBMs is an RG-rich region, followed by a central RNA-recognition motif (RRM) domain, and a second RG-rich region (Gromadzka et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation describing ALYREF domain organization.

claim: A homology model of UAP56 bound to RNA, an ATP-analog, and the C-terminal ALYREF UBM (C-UBM) was prepared based on a yeast crystal structure.
source: To gain insight into ALYREF function, we prepared a homology model of UAP56 bound to RNA, an ATP-analog, and the C-terminal ALYREF UBM (C-UBM) based on a yeast crystal structure (Ren et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes the modeling approach used.

claim: The homology model was superimposed onto the human THO–UAP56 tetramer structure via the four UAP56 RecA2 lobes.
source: We then superimposed this model onto the human THO–UAP56 tetramer structure via the four UAP56 RecA2 lobes (Figure 4b, Figure 4—figure supplement 1d,e).
evidence: This describes the modeling approach used.

claim: A single ALYREF protein may reach across the two THO dimers to bind two juxtaposed UAP56 helicases.
source: First, the model suggests that a single ALYREF protein may reach across the two THO dimers to bind two juxtaposed UAP56 helicases.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the structural model.

claim: The ALYREF N- and C-UBMs would each bind one UAP56 RecA1 lobe, located 20 Å apart, from THO–UAP56 monomers 1A and 2B (or 2A and 1B).
source: The ALYREF N- and C-UBMs would each bind one UAP56 RecA1 lobe (Hautbergue et al., 2009), located 20 Å apart, from THO–UAP56 monomers 1A and 2B (or 2A and 1B) (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the structural model and known UBM binding properties.

claim: ALYREF could bridge two UAP56 proteins within one dimer, which are ~200 Å apart, or possibly multiple THO–UAP56 tetramers.
source: Alternatively, ALYREF could bridge two UAP56 proteins within one dimer, which are ~200 Å apart, or possibly multiple THO–UAP56 tetramers.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the structural model.

claim: Bridging by ALYREF can explain why deletion of either N- or C-UBM leads to growth defects in yeast.
source: Bridging by ALYREF can explain why deletion of either N- or C-UBM leads to growth defects in yeast (Strässer and Hurt, 2001; Zenklusen et al., 2001) and suggests that the UBMs and associated RG-rich domains contribute to the avidity of TREX–mRNA binding, consistent with biochemical data (Hautbergue et al., 2008; Ren et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural model and supported by citations to genetic and biochemical data.

claim: The UBMs and associated RG-rich domains contribute to the avidity of TREX–mRNA binding.
source: Bridging by ALYREF can explain why deletion of either N- or C-UBM leads to growth defects in yeast (Strässer and Hurt, 2001; Zenklusen et al., 2001) and suggests that the UBMs and associated RG-rich domains contribute to the avidity of TREX–mRNA binding, consistent with biochemical data (Hautbergue et al., 2008; Ren et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an inference supported by citations to biochemical data.

claim: RNA binding by UAP56 would orient the mobile RecA1 lobe and project conserved negatively charged residues of the interacting ALYREF UBM towards a conserved patch of positively charged residues of the juxtaposed UAP56 RecA2 lobe.
source: Furthermore, RNA binding by UAP56 (monomers 1A and 2A) would orient the mobile RecA1 lobe and project conserved negatively charged residues of the interacting ALYREF UBM towards a conserved patch of positively charged residues of the juxtaposed UAP56 RecA2 lobe (from monomers 1B and 2B) (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the structural model and charge complementarity.

claim: The UAP56 RecA2 surface is frequently bound by regulators in other DEXD-box helicases.
source: This RecA2 surface is frequently bound by regulators in other DEXD-box helicases (Linder and Jankowsky, 2011; Buchwald et al., 2013; Sharif et al., 2013; Mathys et al., 2014; Figure 4—figure supplement 1g) and suggests how a single UBM could be sufficient for partial ALYREF function (Strässer and Hurt, 2001; Zenklusen et al., 2001; Golovanov et al., 2006; Gromadzka et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies of other DEXD-box helicases.

claim: A single UBM could be sufficient for partial ALYREF function.
source: This RecA2 surface is frequently bound by regulators in other DEXD-box helicases (Linder and Jankowsky, 2011; Buchwald et al., 2013; Sharif et al., 2013; Mathys et al., 2014; Figure 4—figure supplement 1g) and suggests how a single UBM could be sufficient for partial ALYREF function (Strässer and Hurt, 2001; Zenklusen et al., 2001; Golovanov et al., 2006; Gromadzka et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural observations and supported by citations to genetic studies.

claim: The ALYREF UBMs bridge UAP56 helicases, which may correctly position other ALYREF regions for export factor loading.
source: Notably, these two models of ALYREF function are not mutually exclusive and collectively suggest that the ALYREF UBMs bridge UAP56 helicases, which may correctly position other ALYREF regions for export factor loading.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the structural model.

claim: The functionally related ALYREF-like proteins contain one (LUZP4, POLDIP3, UIF) or two (CHTOP) closely spaced UBMs.
source: The functionally related ALYREF-like proteins contain one (LUZP4, POLDIP3, UIF) or two (CHTOP) closely spaced UBMs (Gromadzka et al., 2016; Hautbergue et al., 2009; Viphakone et al., 2015; Figure 4—figure supplement 1c), and thus are unlikely to bridge two helicase RecA1 lobes in the THO–UAP56 structure (Figure 4—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural model and supported by citations describing ALYREF-like proteins.

claim: The THO–UAP56 tetramer increases the affinity of mRNA-export adaptors to their target mRNAs through avidity, by providing multiple UAP56 binding sites in close proximity.
source: Nevertheless, we speculate that the THO–UAP56 tetramer increases the affinity of mRNA-export adaptors to their target mRNAs through avidity, by providing multiple UAP56 binding sites in close proximity.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as speculation.

claim: UAP56 is a member of the DEXD-box RNA helicase family.
source: UAP56 is a member of the DEXD-box RNA helicase family.
evidence: This is established knowledge about UAP56.

claim: DEXD-box helicases function as 'clampases' that couple ATP hydrolysis to RNA release and can be regulated by interacting proteins.
source: These helicases function as 'clampases' that couple ATP hydrolysis to RNA release and can be regulated by interacting proteins (Linder and Jankowsky, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation describing DEXD-box helicase function.

claim: Biochemical data from yeast and humans show that ALYREF weakly promotes UAP56 ATPase activity.
source: Biochemical data from yeast (Ren et al., 2017) and humans (Taniguchi and Ohno, 2008; Shen et al., 2007) show that ALYREF weakly promotes UAP56 ATPase activity, and the yeast THO complex further stimulates this (Ren et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to biochemical studies.

claim: The yeast THO complex further stimulates UAP56 ATPase activity.
source: Biochemical data from yeast (Ren et al., 2017) and humans (Taniguchi and Ohno, 2008; Shen et al., 2007) show that ALYREF weakly promotes UAP56 ATPase activity, and the yeast THO complex further stimulates this (Ren et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to biochemical studies.

claim: The human THOC1/2/3 core complex is sufficient to promote UAP56 ATPase activity in vitro.
source: We observed that the human THOC1/2/3 core complex is sufficient to promote UAP56 ATPase activity in vitro, consistent with our structure and other MIF4G–DEXD-box helicase systems (Hilbert et al., 2011; Montpetit et al., 2011; Figure 4—figure supplement 2a,b).
evidence: This is supported by biochemical data presented in the manuscript.

claim: THO and ALYREF regulate the activity of two bridged UAP56 helicases within the TREX–mRNA complex to control export factor loading onto mRNA.
source: Taken together, we propose that THO and ALYREF regulate the activity of two bridged UAP56 helicases within the TREX–mRNA complex to control export factor loading onto mRNA (Hautbergue et al., 2008; Taniguchi and Ohno, 2008).
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the structural and biochemical data, supported by citations.

claim: A previously reported 6.0 Å resolution crystal structure of the six-subunit yeast Sc THO–Sub2 complex was re-analyzed.
source: To gain insights into conservation of the TREX complex, we re-analyzed a previously reported 6.0 Å resolution crystal structure of the six-subunit yeast Sc THO–Sub2 complex (Ren et al., 2017; Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the re-analysis of a published structure.

claim: The yeast THO–Sub2 structure was proposed to be a six-subunit monomer, within which a single Tex1 (THOC3) and a single Sub2 (UAP56) subunit were assigned, but not Tho2, Hpr1, Thp2, or Mft1.
source: The yeast structure was proposed to be a six-subunit monomer, within which a single Tex1 (THOC3) and a single Sub2 (UAP56) subunit were assigned, but not Tho2, Hpr1, Thp2, or Mft1.
evidence: This describes the original interpretation of the yeast structure.

claim: The revised yeast model revealed that the crystal contained a 12-subunit THO–Sub2 dimer.
source: Surprisingly, our revised yeast model revealed that the crystal contained a 12-subunit THO–Sub2 dimer, which could better explain the published electron density and phosphotungsten cluster positions (Figure 4—figure supplement 3a–c, Video 2).
evidence: This is based on re-analysis of the published crystal structure data.

claim: Two copies of Tho2, Hpr1, the Thp2–Mft1 coiled coil, and one additional copy of the Tex1 and Sub2 subunits were assigned in the revised yeast model.
source: We could assign two copies of Tho2, Hpr1, the Thp2–Mft1 coiled coil, and place one additional copy of the Tex1 and Sub2 subunits based on (i) comparisons to the human THO–UAP56 structure, (ii) the known homologies of yeast Hpr1, Tho2, Tex1, and Mft1 with human THOC1, −2,–3, and −7, and (iii) the predicted Thp2 coiled coil (Söding et al., 2005; Figure 4—figure supplement 3d, Materials and methods).
evidence: This is based on re-analysis of the published crystal structure data using the human structure as a guide.

claim: The revised model allowed identification of Thp2 and confirmation of Mft1 as the respective yeast homologs of the THOC5 and THOC7 coiled coils.
source: The revised model allowed us to identify Thp2 and confirm Mft1 as the respective yeast homologs of the THOC5 and THOC7 coiled coils.
evidence: This is based on re-analysis of the published crystal structure data.

claim: There is an unexpectedly high degree of structural conservation of the five-subunit THO complex monomer (THOC1, −2, –3, −5, –7) and its dimerization via coiled coils between yeast and humans.
source: This indicates an unexpectedly high degree of structural conservation of the five-subunit THO complex monomer (THOC1, −2, –3, −5, –7) and its dimerization via coiled coils.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of the human and revised yeast structures.

claim: The THO–Sub2 model shows that the two Sub2 helicases are located ~80 Å apart.
source: Notably, the THO–Sub2 model shows that the two Sub2 helicases are located ~80 Å apart.
evidence: This is a measurement from the revised yeast model.

claim: Both Sub2 helicases bind to their respective Tho2 MIF4G domain in monomers A and B, analogous to the human THOC2–UAP56 interaction.
source: Both bind to their respective Tho2 MIF4G domain in monomers A and B, analogous to the human THOC2–UAP56 interaction.
evidence: This is an observation from the revised yeast model.

claim: In yeast, a single Yra1 could bridge two Sub2 helicases via its N- and C-UBM regions, mirroring human ALYREF.
source: Thus, also in yeast a single Yra1 could bridge two Sub2 helicases via its N- and C-UBM regions, mirroring human ALYREF (Figure 4—figure supplement 3d).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the revised yeast model and analogy to the human system.

claim: THO–UAP56 forms a dimer in yeast and a constitutive tetramer in humans.
source: Our results suggest a unified model for TREX function through multimerization of the THO–UAP56 complex (Figure 4c). THO–UAP56 forms a dimer in yeast (Figure 4—figure supplement 3) and a constitutive tetramer in humans, mediated by the additional THOC5 tRWD domain and THOC6 subunit (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1f–h, Figure 4—figure supplement 3f).
evidence: This is based on the structural data from both human and yeast complexes.

claim: Human THO–UAP56 tetramerization is mediated by the additional THOC5 tRWD domain and THOC6 subunit.
source: Our results suggest a unified model for TREX function through multimerization of the THO–UAP56 complex (Figure 4c). THO–UAP56 forms a dimer in yeast (Figure 4—figure supplement 3) and a constitutive tetramer in humans, mediated by the additional THOC5 tRWD domain and THOC6 subunit (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1f–h, Figure 4—figure supplement 3f).
evidence: This is based on the structural data showing the role of THOC5 tRWD and THOC6 in tetramerization.

claim: THO–UAP56 tetramerization may have evolved in humans in response to an increased complexity in gene architecture and mRNP composition.
source: In humans, THO–UAP56 tetramerization may have evolved in response to an increased complexity in gene architecture and mRNP composition (Singh et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculation about evolutionary adaptation, supported by citation.

claim: The conserved THO–UAP56 multimerization, extended architecture, and flexibility indicate that one complex can bind multiple mRNP maturation marks and mRNA regions simultaneously.
source: The conserved THO–UAP56 multimerization, extended architecture, and flexibility (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b–d, Figure 4—figure supplement 1d) indicate that one complex can bind multiple mRNP maturation marks and mRNA regions simultaneously.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural features observed.

claim: Subsequent to THO–UAP56 recruitment to the mRNP, a single ALYREF (or yeast Yra1) molecule could bridge two juxtaposed UAP56–mRNA complexes.
source: Subsequent to THO–UAP56 recruitment to the mRNP, a single ALYREF (or yeast Yra1) molecule could bridge two juxtaposed UAP56–mRNA complexes and, potentially, multimerize itself through its RG-rich regions (Gromadzka et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the structural model.

claim: ALYREF could potentially multimerize itself through its RG-rich regions.
source: Subsequent to THO–UAP56 recruitment to the mRNP, a single ALYREF (or yeast Yra1) molecule could bridge two juxtaposed UAP56–mRNA complexes and, potentially, multimerize itself through its RG-rich regions (Gromadzka et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculation supported by citation.

claim: In the assembled TREX–mRNP complex UAP56 ATPase activity is stimulated.
source: In the assembled TREX–mRNP complex UAP56 ATPase activity is stimulated and, together with ALYREF or alternative export adaptors, may load the export factor NXF1–NXT1 from multiple sites within the complex.
evidence: This is based on biochemical data and the structural model.

claim: UAP56, together with ALYREF or alternative export adaptors, may load the export factor NXF1–NXT1 from multiple sites within the complex.
source: In the assembled TREX–mRNP complex UAP56 ATPase activity is stimulated and, together with ALYREF or alternative export adaptors, may load the export factor NXF1–NXT1 from multiple sites within the complex.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the structural model and biochemical data.

claim: Requirements for both the selectivity and efficiency of mRNP recognition and mRNA-export licensing are fulfilled through multivalent interactions between proteins and mRNA.
source: Taken together, the data support a model where requirements for both the selectivity and efficiency of mRNP recognition and mRNA-export licensing are fulfilled through multivalent interactions between proteins and mRNA.
evidence: This is the overall conclusion/model proposed based on all the data presented.
